newsitem.title: USA: Cambodia's Hun Sen vows action to capture Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen vows action to capture Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Sen said in a television interview on Wednesday that last week's trial of former Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot was "a political farce" and proposed measures to arrest Pol Pot and bring him before an international tribunal.

In an interview with ABC-TV's "Nightline" programme, Hun Sen said his two-stage plan called for the Cambodian government to gain control of the Anlong Ven area, Pol Pot's headquarters, through Khmer Rouge defections and "military measures."

Hun Sen, who once served as a brigade commander in the guerrilla movement, also said he would discuss with the Thai government the possibility of cooperating to capture Pol Pot and other Khmer Rouge officials.
Hun Sen spoke to ABC after viewing a videotape of the show trial of Pol Pot in northern Cambodia last week where he was condemned and sentenced to life in detention for his crimes.
Pol Pot, now almost 70, was responsible for the death of more than 1 million people during the Khmer Rouge's "killing fields" rule from 1975-79.
"I want to send him to international court because this is the big problem: genocide problem," Hun Sen told ABC, speaking in English.
"This is for the Cambodian people as well as for the whole world, to prevent genocide. Therefore, I don't think just because Pol Pot dies we don't have a trial."

White House officials have been quoted as saying that Hun Sen, who ousted his royalist co-premier, Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 in a bloody takeover, could rehabilitate his reputation by turning Pol Pot over.
"We have to do everything to reflect the truth," Hun Sen told ABC. "For the world as well as Cambodia, we have to stay in the light. We have to wash our faces and our body in front of the law."
